newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps led higher by mogas, naphtha, CFDs.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps led higher by mogas, naphtha, CFDs.

text.p: European oil swaps were on Thursday traded much higher on gasoline and naphtha, were flat on fuel oil and gas oil differentials and fell back slightly on jet, dealers said.

Brent crude CFDs were earlier traded for August 18-22 at -$0.25 and -$0.23 before surging to around $0.15, while following week talk strengthened to -$0.18 against -$0.25/-$0.30 Wednesday and around -$0.23 earlier Thursday.
Front month gas oil cracks were seen notionally slightly up on strong early screen gains, but no change was noted by brokers on the outer quarters.

Brokers dismissed claims by one oil major that EN590 had been more aggressively offered Thursday than it had been for two weeks and was $0.50 down on the day, saying that gas oil differentials remained broadly unchanged.
Indeed, despite earlier failed attempts to strike a September EN590 deal at $8.50, brokers placed latest values in the $8.25-$9.00 range, a touch up on the day.

On an otherwise extremely quiet day on both the gas oil and fuel oil swaps markets, a fresh jet trade was registered at $24.25 premium for fourth quarter, underlining the third consecutive $0.25 daily decline on jet differentials.
A high/low fuel oil spread trade for the fourth quarter was earlier seen at $5.25 as one dealer said the market had been "quiet as a grave" both on- and off-screen in the absence of price volatility.
Friday's Ascension day holiday is expected to produce another extremely quiet day given the impact on Med countries in particular, a trader said.

Gasoline swaps rose $4.50 on September, te most actively talked month, on higher screen values and barge deals, with August swaps seen traded at $223.50, September at $204.50, Sep/Oct at $11 and the September crack at $5.18.
Naphtha was $1-$1.50 higher on barely-talked August and around $2 up on September in line with higher futures levels and high-priced recent physical trades.
Septemebr trades were rumoured done up to $188.50 in earlier activity before values rose to around $190, while an earlier Sep/Oct spread trade was seen at $1.50.
